newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SPIRLEA ELIMINATES SANCHEZ VICARIO AT EVERT CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPIRLEA ELIMINATES SANCHEZ VICARIO AT EVERT CUP.

text.p: Top seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario's quest for her first tournament title since last May will have to wait now that sixth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania pushed her aside 4-6 6-3 6-3 Thursday in the semifinals of the Evert Cup.
The 11th-ranked Spirlea's win in the only match of the day was her third consecutive victory over the fourth-ranked Sanchez Vicario after losing to the Spaniard the first two times they played.
Spirlea will play the winner of Friday's all-American semifinal match-up between fourth seed Lindsay Davenport and ninth seed Mary Joe Fernandez.
By reaching the semifinals here Spirlea's guaranteed a career high ranking of ninth come Monday morning.
Sanchez Vicario has captured 24 career titles, but Spirlea is no stranger to winning tournaments herself. This Saturday will mark Spirlea's eighth visit to a tour final. She has won four titles.
Sanchez Vicario used to be known for her consistency, but not lately. Against Spirlea she sprayed 30 unforced errors all over the place -- into the net and beyond the boundaries of the court.
In addition, Sanchez Vicario ended the one hour, 59 minute match with a slim 15 outright winners.
"I think she's a good player and she has a very good forehand," Sanchez Vicario said. "She's improved a lot lately."
Although Spirlea posted 50 unforced errors, she reduced her mistakes with each successive set. And she had more than double the number of winners than Sqanchez Vicario: 34.
Spirlea started slowly because of inexperience under the lights. She could not recall playing a night match before.

"I had problems to see the ball," Spirlea said. "When I came on the court, I was like, you know, it's too dark out there. I never played a night match. Maybe I played one. Well, I know that it's night, but I was expecting like more light or something."
In the second set, Spirlea went ahead 3-0, but Sanchez Vicario won the next two games. Spirlea broke the Spaniard's serve in the sixth game for a 4-2 lead.
"I think she lost her concentration after she lost the second set," Spirlea said. "I mean, I was up four-love. She missed a few easy shots, so she was confused."

Spirlea raced to a 4-0 lead in the final set. Although Sanchez Vicario broke Sprilea's serve in the sixth game, it was not enough to fight her way back. Spirlea won two of the last three games of the match.
"I had some opportunities to get close, but at the end, she just went for it a little bit more than me," Sanchez Vicario said. "She took the advantage."
